transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel, Jordan Kim (Redwood); Dr. Sara Nguyen, Liam O'Connor, Priya Sharma, Evan Brooks (Halcyon)

Summary:
Short kickoff to align on onboarding plan, security signoffs, test dataset, and performance benchmarking cadence. Agreement to run a 2-week POC in Redwood Dedicated / sandbox with focus on latency and data residency.

Topics:
- Goals and success criteria
- Security / SSO / encryption questions
- Test data and benchmarks
- Deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
- Next steps and owners

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya, your CSM, and Jordan from our SE team is here too. Quick intros?
[00:18] Dr. Sara Nguyen (Halcyon): Hi all, Sara here — lead on clinical models at Halcyon. We're excited to get started.
[00:25] Liam O'Connor (Halcyon): Liam, CTO. We're evaluating Redwood for inference on our triage models, mostly latency and PHI controls.
[00:34] Jordan Kim (Redwood): Great — thanks. Quick note: we'll go over onboarding steps, security, and then a proposed bench plan.
[00:45] Priya Sharma (Halcyon): Priya, ops — we'll be owning infra and network. Questions on VPC and KMS up front.
[00:52] Maya: Perfect. High level: our typical kickoff is a sandbox on Redwood Dedicated (or Private if you need air-gap), we'll run sample inference, then do a benchmark run and validation.
[01:10] Evan Brooks (Halcyon): What's the difference again between Dedicated and Private? Just the network?
[01:18] Jordan: Yeah, Dedicated is reserved GPU pools in our cloud with tenant isolation; Private is customer-managed VPC or on-prem package — more control, more ops.
[01:28] Dr. Nguyen: For PHI we need KMS integration and audit logs retention for 1 year, plus SSO. Can Redwood do HSM-backed keys?
[01:40] Jordan: Yes, we support KMS/HSM integrations — we can plug into AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and for Private deployments we support customer HSM. Audit logs and enhanced retention are part of our enterprise add-on.
[01:54] Liam: Is there a SOC2 / ISO cert we can share with procurement?
[02:01] Maya: We'll send the security pack after the call — SOC 2 Type II report, ISO docs, network diagrams. I'll include it in the onboarding folder.
[02:09] Priya: Also need SAML SSO, and RBAC mapping to our groups.
[02:16] Jordan: We support SAML SSO and mapping roles; there are sometimes small name mangles with group attributes but we can test in the sandbox.
[02:27] Dr. Nguyen: On performance, our target is sub-150ms 95th percentile for the triage model at 512 tokens. Is that realistic?
[02:40] Jordan: Depends on model and quantization. For popular open models we often hit under 100ms on p3/p4-type hardware with our optimized kernels, but for larger seqs it can increase. We can run a benchmark with your model and sequence profile.
[02:56] Liam: We'll probably need batching to save cost; how does Redwood handle batching vs latency?
[03:03] Jordan: Smart routing and continuous batching — we tune batch size to maintain latency SLOs. For strict tail latency we can pin dedicated slots and reduce batching. There's always a tradeoff cost vs latency.
[03:18] Priya: About data — can we store logs only in our region? Data residency is important for compliance.
[03:25] Maya: Yes, for Dedicated and Private we can provision region-specific endpoints and restrict logs. Hosted API has region controls but dedicated/private give more guarantee.
[03:35] Evan: Any known gotchas when pulling model KV cache over network? We saw earlier folks call it KV 'cash' in notes.
[03:44] Jordan: (laughs) Yeah, KV cache — we manage the KV cache in-memory on the serving nodes. For Private deployments we keep it in-cluster. No network calls for KV during generation once warmed.
[03:58] Dr. Nguyen: Security questionnaire — can we get a timeline? Procurement wants answers within a week.
[04:05] Maya: I'll push the security pack and questionnaire today, can you commit to returning it by Friday?
[04:12] Liam: Yes, we'll aim for that.
[04:18] Jordan: For the POC plan we suggest three phases: 1) Sandbox provisioning and sample run (this week), 2) Benchmarking with your model and dataset (week 2), 3) Validation and rollout plan — can be canaryed to small traffic.
[04:34] Priya: Who will provision the sandbox? We need network peering details and maybe a dedicated VPC.
[04:41] Maya: We'll provision and share a sandbox project and invite your team. For VPC peering / Private we'll coordinate network diagrams — Jordan will send the network checklist.
[04:52] Evan: On costs — rough order magnitude for dedicated nodes? We need to include in budget.
[04:58] Maya: I'll include sample pricing tiers in the follow-up. For POC we normally provide a time-limited sandbox at reduced rate.
[05:08] Dr. Nguyen: Any limitations on model sizes or quantization support? We plan to run a 13B model with int8 quantization.
[05:15] Jordan: We support a range of quantizations — int8/int4 for certain architectures, but accuracy regressions can happen. We'll recommend quantization profiles after seeing samples.
[05:28] Liam: Are there existing connectors for our telemetry stack? We use Datadog and internal logging.
[05:35] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Console exports metrics; we can push traces to Datadog and set up token-level cost and latency breakdowns.
[05:44] Priya: On network egress — any concerns for PHI?
[05:48] Maya: For PHI we recommend Dedicated or Private; Hosted API can be used but must be configured for data residency and retention, and we recommend encryption at rest with your KMS keys.
[06:00] Dr. Nguyen: Great. Can we get an initial timeline?
[06:03] Maya: Proposed: sandbox provision by 11/04, return security questionnaire by 11/06, first benchmark slot week of 11/08. Does that work?
[06:13] Liam: Yes that aligns with our internal schedule.
[06:17] Evan: Who else from Redwood should we loop in?
[06:20] Maya: I'll add our infra ops lead if we need deeper Private deployment help. Jordan will handle the bench config and tests.
[06:28] Jordan: I'll also share our benchmark harness — it's a small repo and a spreadsheet for tail latency / throughput.
[06:35] Dr. Nguyen: For the benchmark we'll need to run with our dataset — any constraints on PII?
[06:41] Jordan: You can scrub or use a synthetic subset; for Private Dedicated you can provide real data under NDA. We'll follow your compliance rules.
[06:51] Priya: Can Redwood integrate with our KMS for key rotation? We have quarterly rotation.
[06:58] Jordan: Yes, KMS integrations support rotation; for Private we can map to your HSM policies.
[07:06] Maya: Ok, quick recap of next steps — I'll send onboarding deck, security docs, and create the onboarding folder with links. Jordan will send the benchmark checklist and test harness. Halcyon will provide sample data and security responses.
[07:23] Dr. Nguyen: Sounds good. One last question: if we need to move to Private later, how seamless is migration?
[07:31] Jordan: We design the API & config to be consistent across Hosted, Dedicated, Private. You'd need some network work, but models and config can be ported; some infra changes are required but we have migration guides.
[07:45] Liam: Ok. Thanks everyone.
[07:48] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up with notes and tasks.
[07:52] (meeting ends)

References shared during call:
- Onboarding deck link: https://redwood.example.com/onboarding/halcyon-deck
- Security pack (will be attached in follow-up): /links/sec-pack-halcyon.pdf
- Benchmark harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness

Notes about transcription: occasional speaker swaps and minor word errors (e.g., KV cache transcribed as 'KV cash', "Redwood Dedicated" heard as "Redwood Dedicate").

End of transcript.
